text:
eve_support: Customer (AcmeCorp) reporting regression in p95/p99 for streaming calls vs non-streaming. They say streaming TTFB is high (~600-900ms) while non-streaming total is ~300-400ms. Escalating for triage.

sam_sre: ack — can you paste a minimal repro request and customer region/route?

eve_support: sent DM with route and example: POST /v1/generate?stream=true header Accept: text/event-stream. customer sees first event delayed. Link to customer recording: https://acme.screencast/stream-ttfb-3m

lia_engineer: quick hypothesis: proxy coalescing + edge keepalive interaction causing delayed flush for small initial chunks. Also need to know model variant and sequence length distribution.

alex_prod: is this new after the latest runtime kernel selector rollout? we did a small change to batching thresholds last week. could be related.

sam_sre: collecting kernel-rollout id and route config now. eve — what SDK and client path (browser vs server)?

eve_support: customer uses server SDK (node) via our hosted API, SDK 1.4.2. They have `stream=true` and small prompt size (~30 tokens).

lia_engineer: small prompts + streaming can hit our coalescing window: runtime waits to aggregate small chunks before flush to maximize throughput. For p99 this can add ~+500ms if coalesce window is 200-500ms. We have heuristics that bypass for explicit immediate-flush flags but SDK doesn't set it by default.

sam_sre: can we repro internally? I'll run a curl that mimics their headers and add request timings.

sam_sre: repro command: ```bash
curl -i -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -d '{"input":"short prompt"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?stream=true
```

lia_engineer: run with env DEBUG=flush to get server-side flush logs. Also check edge proxy logs for ``proxy_flush_delay_ms`` metric.

sam_sre: ran repro against prod-route, attaching simplified logs: 
```
[12:03:01.001] req start
[12:03:01.050] model first-token gen 40ms
[12:03:01.051] kv-cache write
[12:03:01.550] runtime coalesce flush (window=500ms) -> client chunk send
[12:03:01.551] client first byte
```

sam_sre: shows model generated quickly but runtime waited ~500ms to flush.

alex_prod: that matches the new batching thresholds. For tiny prompts we should either bypass coalesce (immediate flush) or drop window to 50ms for streaming routes.

lia_engineer: propose short-term mitigation: rollout a per-route override to set coalesce_window_ms=50 for public streaming endpoints. Long-term: SDK should set immediate-flush for interactive patterns; consider adaptive window based on prompt length and client RTT.

eve_support: customer asked for quick workaround — would switching to non-streaming endpoint help? They see non-streaming faster overall currently.

sam_sre: yes non-streaming aggregates at runtime and returns full response as soon as model completes; it bypasses coalesce behavior that waits for multiple tokens. For small outputs, non-streaming can be lower-latency. Suggest offering that as a stopgap.

alex_prod: I'll open a safe canary to change coalesce_window_ms for the streaming route on 2 hosts in us-west-2. deploy-bot will post details.

deploy-bot: Scheduled canary: route=public-gen-streaming us-west-2 hosts=[host-7,host-8] change=coalesce_window_ms:500->50 start=2026-04-09T15:00Z canary-id=c-101

lia_engineer: monitoring: add quick dashboards for p95/p99 streaming TTFB and proxy_flush_delay_ms before/after. Also add alert for regression >150ms on p95.

sam_sre: action items: 1) canary w/ reduced window (alex) 2) SDK ticket to set immediate-flush for short prompts (lia) 3) customer outreach with workaround (eve) 4) telemetry dashboard (sam).

eve_support: looping in customer now with suggested workaround (use non-streaming or wait for our canary). Customer asked for ETA — can we target same-day canary?

alex_prod: can try same-day if no CI issues. starting canary now, will update.

deploy-bot: Canary started: c-101 progress=0/2 hosts updated

sam_sre: I'll keep watch on the metrics and post p95 numbers in thread.

(ended)
